execution_boundary.summary: OSCAL represents controls and assessment artifacts rather than executing governed transitions.

preparation_boundary.summary: OSCAL may document controls around preparation but does not determine or authorize preparation consequence.

commitment_boundary.summary: Versioned control and assessment evidence may inform commitment review through a StegVerse evidence adapter; it is not a commit decision.

semantic_equivalence_boundary.summary: Control identifiers, profile resolution, model version, document version, and transformation semantics require explicit interpretation; schema-validity is not semantic equivalence.

unknown_trajectory_boundary.summary: OSCAL does not directly classify unknown runtime trajectories; missing applicability or unresolved context must fail closed.

authority_boundary.summary: Responsible-party, implementation, and assessment records do not grant current execution authority or delegation.

evidence_freshness_boundary.summary: Model release, document/content version, assessment time, references, and applicability must remain current for the evaluated transition.

reconstruction_boundary.summary: Pinned model/document identities and machine-readable control/assessment records can strengthen reconstruction when references and transformations are retained.

interoperability_path.summary: OSCAL artifacts enter as structured policy/control/assessment evidence; stronger native validator/converter interoperability requires a separately observed tool-execution packet.

next_required_action: canonical merged-state validation of the source-versioned OSCAL 1.2.2 bounded crosswalk; native validator/converter execution is a separate stronger evidence transition, not required for the current source-level terminal class
